speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination and a history of a swollen left ankle. To understand what's happening, I need to ask if you have a history of gout, psoriasis, or any kidney or urinary tract issues.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis.

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (painful urination), and recent sexual activity is highly suggestive of Reiter's syndrome. Given the patient's age and symptoms, I would like to confirm the diagnosis with a urinalysis and test for Chlamydia.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Chlamydia PCR, Rheumatoid Factor, HLA-B27.
